page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.re6p-redis.large is an x86_64 instance provisioned under the KVM hypervisor within the memory-optimized classification. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor alongside 8.0 GB of system memory, providing an even allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. The server includes a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface, does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and does not contain bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Because the server operates without integrated disk storage, workloads require external cloud storage volumes for persistent data retention. From a resource perspective, the dedicated Intel Xeon cores provide stable compute without CPU oversubscription contention. The 1:4 core-to-memory configuration delivers balanced capacity for low-footprint services. Primary workload fits include lightweight in-memory key-value caching such as Redis, small relational databases, staging environments, microservices, and general-purpose background processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.re6p-redis.large is a dual-core x86_64 virtual instance hosted on KVM hypervisors. Driven by 2 dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY vCPUs, it is supplied with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 4.0 GB per vCPU distribution. The instance does not feature onboard local disks, mandating external network-attached storage for system and application persistence. In addition, it operates with zero hardware accelerators, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. With dedicated CPU allocation, the configuration avoids noisy-neighbor contention common to shared-core models, offering consistent execution. Given its modest memory footprint and dual-core topology, this instance profile is suitable for lightweight in-memory caching solutions like Redis, entry-level database hosting, microservice routing, and balanced general-purpose application workloads requiring predictable compute performance.
